text_es: Write a SQL-backed function named `align(gates, jumps)`. The gates data includes a gate identifier, a sector name, and a base stability score. The jumps data tracks a jump identifier, the gate identifier, a misalignment angle, and a jump year. Join the two datasets to calculate the average misalignment angle for each sector name. Only consider jumps that occurred after the year three thousand, and only include gates that have a base stability score below fifty. Group the results by sector name and filter to keep only those sectors where the average misalignment angle is strictly greater than ten. Return a list of tuples containing the sector name and the average misalignment angle, ordered by the angle in descending order. Example input: gates with sector Orion and stability forty, jumps with angles twelve and sixteen. Example output: [("Orion", 14)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE gates (
    gate_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sector_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    base_stability INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE jumps (
    jump_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    gate_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    misalignment_angle INTEGER NOT NULL,
    jump_year INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO gates (gate_id, sector_name, base_stability) VALUES
    (1, 'Orion', 40),
    (2, 'Orion', 45),
    (3, 'Lyra', 70),
    (4, 'Draco', 20),
    (5, 'Vega', 35);

INSERT INTO jumps (jump_id, gate_id, misalignment_angle, jump_year) VALUES
    (100, 1, 12, 3010),
    (101, 1, 16, 3025),
    (102, 2, 14, 2990),
    (103, 3, 40, 3100),
    (104, 4, 30, 3050),
    (105, 4, 2, 3051),
    (106, 5, 4, 3060),
    (107, 9, 11, 3070);

CREATE VIEW align AS
SELECT g.sector_name,
       AVG(j.misalignment_angle) AS avg_angle
FROM gates AS g
JOIN jumps AS j
  ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
WHERE j.jump_year > 3000
  AND g.base_stability < 50
GROUP BY g.sector_name
HAVING AVG(j.misalignment_angle) > 10;

SELECT j.jump_id,
       j.gate_id
FROM jumps AS j
LEFT JOIN gates AS g
  ON g.gate_id = j.gate_id
WHERE g.gate_id IS NULL
ORDER BY j.jump_id;

SELECT g.sector_name,
       g.gate_id,
       COUNT(j.jump_id) AS jump_count,
       MAX(j.misalignment_angle) AS worst_angle,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(j.misalignment_angle) > 10 THEN 'CRITICAL'
           ELSE 'NOMINAL'
       END AS gate_status
FROM gates AS g
JOIN jumps AS j
  ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
WHERE g.base_stability < 50
  AND j.jump_year > 3000
GROUP BY g.sector_name,
         g.gate_id
ORDER BY worst_angle DESC;

WITH sector_volume AS (
    SELECT g.sector_name,
           COUNT(*) AS jump_total
    FROM gates AS g
    JOIN jumps AS j
      ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
    WHERE j.jump_year > 3000
      AND g.base_stability < 50
    GROUP BY g.sector_name
)
SELECT a.sector_name,
       a.avg_angle,
       v.jump_total
FROM align AS a
JOIN sector_volume AS v
  ON v.sector_name = a.sector_name
ORDER BY a.avg_angle DESC;

SELECT sector_name,
       avg_angle
FROM align
ORDER BY avg_angle DESC;

text_es: Implement a SQL-powered function named `armor(suits, battles)`. The suits input provides a suit identifier, a pilot name, and a chassis class. The battles input tracks a battle identifier, the suit identifier, an ablation depth in millimeters, and the number of hits taken. Join the datasets to determine the total ablation depth per pilot name. Restrict the data to heavy chassis class suits and battles where the hits taken were greater than twenty. Group by the pilot name and only include pilots whose total ablation depth is over one hundred millimeters. Return a list of tuples with the pilot name and total ablation depth, sorted by depth descending. Example input: suits piloted by Jax in a heavy chassis, battles with depths of sixty and fifty. Example output: [("Jax", 110)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE suits (
    suit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    pilot_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    chassis_class VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE battles (
    battle_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    suit_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ablation_depth_mm INTEGER NOT NULL,
    hits_taken INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO suits (suit_id, pilot_name, chassis_class) VALUES
    (1, 'Jax', 'heavy'),
    (2, 'Rill', 'heavy'),
    (3, 'Moya', 'light'),
    (4, 'Doran', 'heavy');

INSERT INTO battles (battle_id, suit_id, ablation_depth_mm, hits_taken) VALUES
    (10, 1, 60, 34),
    (11, 1, 50, 22),
    (12, 1, 90, 12),
    (13, 2, 40, 41),
    (14, 2, 30, 25),
    (15, 3, 200, 55),
    (16, 4, 130, 21);

SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
       SUM(b.ablation_depth_mm) AS total_ablation_depth_mm
FROM suits AS s
JOIN battles AS b
    ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
  AND b.hits_taken > 20
GROUP BY s.pilot_name
HAVING SUM(b.ablation_depth_mm) > 100
ORDER BY total_ablation_depth_mm DESC;

SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
       COUNT(*) AS qualifying_battles,
       MAX(b.ablation_depth_mm) AS worst_battle_depth_mm
FROM suits AS s
JOIN battles AS b
    ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
  AND b.hits_taken > 20
GROUP BY s.pilot_name
ORDER BY qualifying_battles DESC;

WITH qualifying AS (
    SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
           b.ablation_depth_mm AS depth_mm,
           b.hits_taken AS hits_taken
    FROM suits AS s
    JOIN battles AS b
        ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
    WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
      AND b.hits_taken > 20
)
SELECT pilot_name,
       SUM(depth_mm) AS total_ablation_depth_mm,
       CASE
           WHEN SUM(depth_mm) > 100 THEN 'critical'
           ELSE 'serviceable'
       END AS armor_status,
       SUM(depth_mm) / SUM(hits_taken) AS depth_per_hit
FROM qualifying
GROUP BY pilot_name
ORDER BY total_ablation_depth_mm DESC;

UPDATE suits
SET chassis_class = 'heavy-refit'
WHERE suit_id IN (
    SELECT b.suit_id
    FROM battles AS b
    WHERE b.hits_taken > 20
      AND b.ablation_depth_mm > 55
);

DELETE FROM battles
WHERE hits_taken <= 20
  AND ablation_depth_mm < 100;

text_es: Write a function using SQL named `grow(reefs, measurements)`. The reefs data lists a reef identifier, an ocean region, and a coral strain. The measurements data tracks a measurement identifier, the reef identifier, a calcium uptake value, and a water acidity level. Join the lists to sum the total calcium uptake for each ocean region. Consider only reefs growing the luminescent coral strain and measurements where the water acidity level was above eight. Group by ocean region and filter for regions where the total calcium uptake exceeds one thousand units. Return a list of tuples containing the ocean region and total calcium uptake, sorted by uptake in descending order. Example input: reefs in the Pacific region with luminescent strain, measurements showing uptakes of six hundred and five hundred. Example output: [("Pacific", 1100)].
text_nat:
CREATE type reef_row AS (reef_id integer, ocean_region text, coral_strain text);

CREATE type measurement_row AS (
    measurement_id integer,
    reef_id integer,
    calcium_uptake numeric,
    water_acidity numeric
);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION normalized_strain(strain text)
returns text
language sql
immutable
AS $$
    SELECT lower(btrim(strain));
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION grow(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns TABLE (ocean_region text, total_calcium_uptake numeric)
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        r.ocean_region,
        sum(m.calcium_uptake)
    FROM unnest(reefs)
        AS r
    JOIN unnest(measurements)
        AS m
        ON m.reef_id = r.reef_id
    WHERE normalized_strain(r.coral_strain) = 'luminescent'
      AND m.water_acidity > 8
    GROUP BY r.ocean_region
    HAVING sum(m.calcium_uptake) > 1000
    ORDER BY sum(m.calcium_uptake) DESC;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION reef_contributions(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns TABLE (reef_id integer, ocean_region text, reef_uptake numeric)
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        r.reef_id,
        r.ocean_region,
        sum(m.calcium_uptake)
    FROM unnest(reefs)
        AS r
    JOIN unnest(measurements)
        AS m
        ON m.reef_id = r.reef_id
    WHERE normalized_strain(r.coral_strain) = 'luminescent'
      AND m.water_acidity > 8
    GROUP BY
        r.reef_id,
        r.ocean_region
    ORDER BY sum(m.calcium_uptake) DESC;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION region_report(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns setof text
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        g.ocean_region || ': ' || to_char(g.total_calcium_uptake, 'FM999999990.9')
    FROM grow(reefs, measurements)
        AS g
    ORDER BY g.total_calcium_uptake DESC;
$$;

CREATE VIEW sample_survey AS
SELECT
    array[
        row(1, 'Pacific', 'luminescent')::reef_row,
        row(2, 'Pacific', 'Luminescent')::reef_row,
        row(3, 'Atlantic', 'stony')::reef_row
    ] AS reefs,
    array[
        row(1, 1, 600, 8.4)::measurement_row,
        row(2, 2, 500, 8.9)::measurement_row,
        row(3, 1, 900, 7.5)::measurement_row,
        row(4, 3, 4000, 8.6)::measurement_row
    ] AS measurements;

SELECT rep.line
FROM sample_survey
    AS s
CROSS JOIN LATERAL region_report(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS rep(line);

SELECT
    c.reef_id,
    c.ocean_region,
    c.reef_uptake
FROM sample_survey
    AS s
CROSS JOIN LATERAL reef_contributions(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS c
JOIN grow(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS g
    ON g.ocean_region = c.ocean_region
ORDER BY c.reef_uptake DESC;

text_es: Implement a function utilizing SQL named `empathize(androids, behaviors)`. The androids table has an android identifier, an occupation role, and a matrix version. The behaviors table tracks a behavior identifier, the android identifier, an empathy score, and an anomaly flag. Join the tables to calculate the average empathy score for each occupation role. Filter for androids running matrix version three and behaviors where the anomaly flag is set to true. Group by occupation role and retain only roles where the average empathy score is strictly less than fifty. Return a list of tuples containing the occupation role and average empathy score, ordered ascending by the empathy score. Example input: androids in a Medic role on version three, behaviors with anomaly flags and empathy scores of forty and forty-six. Example output: [("Medic", 43)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE androids (
    android_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    occupation_role VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    matrix_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE behaviors (
    behavior_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    android_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    empathy_score INTEGER NOT NULL,
    anomaly_flag BOOLEAN NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO androids (android_id, occupation_role, matrix_version) VALUES
    (1, 'Medic', 3),
    (2, 'Medic', 3),
    (3, 'Pilot', 3),
    (4, 'Miner', 2);

INSERT INTO behaviors (behavior_id, android_id, empathy_score, anomaly_flag) VALUES
    (10, 1, 40, TRUE),
    (11, 2, 46, TRUE),
    (12, 2, 88, FALSE),
    (13, 3, 71, TRUE),
    (14, 4, 12, TRUE),
    (15, 9, 20, TRUE);

DELETE FROM behaviors
WHERE android_id NOT IN (SELECT android_id FROM androids);

CREATE VIEW empathize AS
SELECT a.occupation_role,
       AVG(b.empathy_score) AS average_empathy
FROM androids AS a
JOIN behaviors AS b
  ON b.android_id = a.android_id
WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
  AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
GROUP BY a.occupation_role
HAVING AVG(b.empathy_score) < 50;

SELECT occupation_role,
       average_empathy
FROM empathize
ORDER BY average_empathy;

SELECT e.occupation_role,
       e.average_empathy,
       COUNT(b.behavior_id) AS anomaly_count,
       MIN(b.empathy_score) AS lowest_score
FROM empathize AS e
JOIN androids AS a
  ON a.occupation_role = e.occupation_role
JOIN behaviors AS b
  ON b.android_id = a.android_id
WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
  AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
GROUP BY e.occupation_role,
         e.average_empathy
ORDER BY anomaly_count DESC;

WITH flagged AS (
    SELECT a.android_id,
           a.occupation_role,
           b.empathy_score
    FROM androids AS a
    JOIN behaviors AS b
      ON b.android_id = a.android_id
    WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
      AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
)
SELECT f.android_id,
       f.occupation_role,
       f.empathy_score,
       CASE
           WHEN f.empathy_score < 45 THEN 'recall'
           ELSE 'monitor'
       END AS disposition
FROM flagged AS f
JOIN empathize AS e
  ON e.occupation_role = f.occupation_role
ORDER BY f.empathy_score,
         f.android_id;

text_es: Write a SQL script containing a helper view to filter routines with a difficulty above five, and a main procedure `evaluate(season)` for synchronized swimming data. The database holds a table of teams with their country and coach, and a table of routines with the team, formation difficulty, execution score, and penalty points. The main procedure must use these tables to return the country and total final score for each team in the given season, calculated as difficulty plus execution minus penalties, ordered from highest to lowest score. It must also return a second query identifying coaches whose teams average an execution score below seven and have exactly zero penalties. Example: input 2023 with a team from France scoring 8 difficulty and 9 execution with 0 penalties returns France with 17 points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE teams (
  team_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  country VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
  coach VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE routines (
  routine_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  team_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES teams (team_id),
  season INTEGER NOT NULL,
  formation_difficulty DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL,
  execution_score DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL,
  penalty_points DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW hard_routines
  AS
SELECT routine_id,
       team_id,
       season,
       formation_difficulty,
       execution_score,
       penalty_points
FROM routines
WHERE formation_difficulty > 5;

INSERT INTO teams (team_id, country, coach) VALUES
  (1, 'France', 'Claire Dubois'),
  (2, 'Japan', 'Aiko Tanaka'),
  (3, 'Spain', 'Marta Ruiz'),
  (4, 'Canada', 'Erin Blake');

INSERT INTO routines (routine_id, team_id, season, formation_difficulty, execution_score, penalty_points) VALUES
  (1, 1, 2023, 8.00, 9.00, 0.00),
  (2, 2, 2023, 7.50, 8.00, 0.50),
  (3, 3, 2023, 6.00, 6.50, 0.00),
  (4, 3, 2023, 5.50, 6.20, 0.00),
  (5, 4, 2023, 4.50, 8.00, 0.00),
  (6, 1, 2022, 7.00, 8.50, 1.00);

CREATE PROCEDURE evaluate(IN season INTEGER)
BEGIN
  SELECT t.country,
         SUM(r.formation_difficulty + r.execution_score - r.penalty_points)
           AS final_score
  FROM teams t
  JOIN routines r
    ON r.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE r.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.country
  ORDER BY final_score DESC;

  SELECT t.coach,
         t.country,
         AVG(r.execution_score)
           AS average_execution
  FROM teams t
  JOIN routines r
    ON r.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE r.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.coach,
           t.country
  HAVING AVG(r.execution_score) < 7
     AND SUM(r.penalty_points) = 0
  ORDER BY average_execution;

  SELECT t.country,
         COUNT(h.routine_id)
           AS hard_routine_count
  FROM teams t
  JOIN hard_routines h
    ON h.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE h.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.country
  ORDER BY hard_routine_count DESC;
END;

CALL evaluate(2023);

text_es: Write a SQL script with a helper view to isolate coastal zones deeper than one hundred meters, and a main procedure `monitor(region)` for tracking algae blooms. There is a table of coastal zones with their name and water depth, and a table of bloom events storing the zone, glow intensity, water temperature, and nutrient concentration. The main procedure must combine the tables to return the zone name and the maximum glow intensity for the specified region, looking only at events where water temperature is below twenty degrees and nutrient concentration is above fifty, sorted by highest intensity. It must also provide a list of zones that have an average nutrient concentration below thirty and a glow intensity of exactly zero. Example: region North with a zone of 15 degrees, 60 nutrients, and 80 glow returns North zone with 80 maximum intensity.

CREATE TABLE coastal_zones (

    zone_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,

    water_depth DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL
);

);

CREATE VIEW deep_coastal_zones AS

The database maintains a table of dogs with their name and breed, and a table of race segments tracking the dog, position in the team, pulling force, and segment distance. The procedure should analyze the given race to return the breed and total distance pulled for dogs in the lead position, filtering for segments where the pulling force is at least fifty, grouped by breed and ordered by highest total distance. Additionally, it must output the names of dogs who pulled less than twenty force in the wheel position and have a breed of Husky. Example: race 3 with a Husky in lead pulling 60 force for 15 distance returns Husky with 15 total distance.

Write a SQL script providing a helper view to filter buggies with slick tires, and a main procedure `measure(tournament)` for kite buggy races. The system uses a table of buggies with their model and tire type, and a table of race logs recording the buggy, wind speed, traction coefficient, and wheel sinkage. The main procedure should join the tables to output the tire type and average traction coefficient for the given tournament, only including logs where wind speed is between fifteen and twenty five and wheel sinkage is below five, ordered by the highest average traction. It also needs to list buggy models that achieved a perfect traction coefficient of one while experiencing wind speeds above thirty. Example: tournament 2 with a slick tire buggy at 20 wind speed and 0.8 traction returns slick tire with 0.8 average traction.

Write a SQL script creating a helper view for instruments made of maple wood, and a procedure `evaluate(session)` for instrument maintenance records. The records consist of a table of instruments with their serial number and wood type, and a table of maintenance logs containing the instrument, wheel speed, rosin type, and friction resistance. The procedure must join these tables for the given session to return the wood type and the count of logs where rosin type is dark and wheel speed exceeds one hundred, grouped by wood type and sorted by the highest count. It should also output the serial numbers of instruments that used light rosin and achieved a friction resistance of exactly zero. Example: session 8 with a maple instrument using dark rosin at 120 speed returns maple with a count of 1.

Write a SQL script featuring a helper view to identify non-fiction reading attempts, and a main procedure `score(competition)` for speed reading events. The data includes a table of readers with their name and age group, and a table of reading attempts detailing the reader, book genre, words per minute, and quiz score. The procedure must join the tables for a specific competition to return the age group and average quiz score, filtering for attempts where words per minute is above five hundred, grouped by age group and ordered by highest average score. It must also list the names of readers who scored a perfect one hundred on the quiz while reading fiction books at over three hundred words per minute. Example: competition 1 with a teen reader at 600 words per minute and 90 score returns the teen group with a 90 average.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE readers (
  reader_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  reader_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
  age_group VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE reading_attempts (
  attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  competition_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reader_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  book_genre VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  words_per_minute INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quiz_score INTEGER NOT NULL
);

  (2, 'Jonas Reed', 'adult'),

  (4, 'Peter Vane', 'adult');

  (1, 1, 1, 'fiction', 600, 90),
  (2, 1, 2, 'history', 540, 75),
  (3, 1, 3, 'fiction', 320, 100),
  (4, 1, 4, 'fiction', 480, 100),
  (5, 2, 1, 'biography', 610, 60);

CREATE VIEW non_fiction_attempts
AS
SELECT
  a.attempt_id,
  a.competition_id,
  a.reader_id,
  a.words_per_minute,
  a.quiz_score
FROM
  reading_attempts AS a
WHERE
  a.book_genre <> 'fiction';

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE score(IN competition INTEGER)
BEGIN
  SELECT
    r.age_group,
    AVG(a.quiz_score) AS average_quiz_score
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    reading_attempts AS a
  ON
    a.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    a.competition_id = competition
    AND a.words_per_minute > 500
  GROUP BY
    r.age_group
  ORDER BY
    average_quiz_score DESC;

  SELECT
    r.reader_name
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    reading_attempts AS a
  ON
    a.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    a.competition_id = competition
    AND a.book_genre = 'fiction'
    AND a.words_per_minute > 300
    AND a.quiz_score = 100
  ORDER BY
    r.reader_name;

  SELECT
    r.age_group,
    COUNT(*) AS non_fiction_count,
    AVG(n.words_per_minute) AS average_speed
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    non_fiction_attempts AS n
  ON
    n.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    n.competition_id = competition
  GROUP BY
    r.age_group
  ORDER BY
    average_speed DESC;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL score(1);

text_es: Write a SQL script containing a helper view to select recordings above ninety decibels, and a procedure `calculate(festival)` for yodeling acoustic data. The schema features a table of yodelers with their name and vocal range, and a table of echo recordings storing the yodeler, canyon location, decibel level, and echo delay in seconds. The procedure should process the given festival to return the canyon location and the maximum echo delay, focusing on recordings where the vocal range is falsetto, grouped by canyon and ordered by longest delay. Furthermore, it must return the names of yodelers who produced an echo delay of exactly five seconds at the Grand Canyon with a baritone vocal range. Example: festival 4 with a falsetto yodel at 95 decibels producing a 3 second delay at Echo Peak returns Echo Peak with a 3 second maximum delay.
text_nat:
-- Acoustic data model for a yodeling festival.
CREATE TABLE yodelers (
    yodeler_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    yodeler_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    vocal_range VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE echo_recordings (
    recording_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    festival_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    yodeler_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES yodelers (yodeler_id),
    canyon_location VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    decibel_level INTEGER NOT NULL,
    echo_delay_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (2, 4, 3, 'Echo Peak', 92, 2);

INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (4, 4, 2, 'Grand Canyon', 97, 5);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (5, 4, 4, 'Grand Canyon', 91, 5);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (6, 4, 4, 'Grand Canyon', 99, 4);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (7, 5, 1, 'Echo Peak', 96, 9);

-- Helper view: only recordings louder than ninety decibels are usable.
CREATE VIEW loud_recordings AS
SELECT
    r.recording_id,
    r.festival_id,
    r.yodeler_id,
    r.canyon_location,
    r.decibel_level,
    r.echo_delay_seconds
FROM
    echo_recordings AS r
WHERE
    r.decibel_level > 90;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE calculate(IN festival INTEGER)
BEGIN
    -- Longest falsetto echo per canyon for the requested festival.
    SELECT
        lr.canyon_location,
        MAX(lr.echo_delay_seconds) AS max_echo_delay
    FROM
        loud_recordings AS lr
    JOIN
        yodelers AS y
    ON
        lr.yodeler_id = y.yodeler_id
    WHERE
        lr.festival_id = festival
    AND
        y.vocal_range = 'falsetto'
    GROUP BY
        lr.canyon_location
    ORDER BY
        max_echo_delay DESC;

    -- Baritones with a five second Grand Canyon echo.
    SELECT
        y.yodeler_name,
        lr.canyon_location,
        lr.echo_delay_seconds
    FROM
        loud_recordings AS lr
    JOIN
        yodelers AS y
    ON
        y.yodeler_id = lr.yodeler_id
    WHERE
        lr.festival_id = festival
    AND
        y.vocal_range = 'baritone'
    AND
        lr.canyon_location = 'Grand Canyon'
    AND
        lr.echo_delay_seconds = 5
    ORDER BY
        y.yodeler_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL calculate(4);

text_es: Write a SQL script with a helper view to filter shifts on highly complex chords, and a procedure `analyze(recital)` for guitar performance metrics. The database holds a table of guitarists with their name and experience level, and a table of chord shifts tracking the guitarist, song name, chord complexity, and transition time in milliseconds. The procedure must join the tables for a specific recital to return the experience level and the average transition time, including only shifts where the song name is Girl from Ipanema, grouped by experience level and ordered by fastest average time. It should also output the names of guitarists who achieved a transition time of under fifty milliseconds on medium complexity chords. Example: recital 9 with a veteran guitarist transitioning in 120 milliseconds on high complexity returns the veteran level with a 120 average time.
text_nat:
-- Guitar performance metrics: schema, a helper view for highly complex chords,
-- and the analyze(recital) procedure that reports the two result sets.

CREATE TABLE guitarists (
    guitarist_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    experience_level VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE chord_shifts (
    shift_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    recital_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    guitarist_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    song_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    chord_complexity VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    transition_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW complex_chord_shifts AS
SELECT s.shift_id,
       s.recital_id,
       s.song_name,
       s.transition_ms,
       g.name AS guitarist_name,
       g.experience_level
FROM chord_shifts s
    JOIN guitarists g
        ON g.guitarist_id = s.guitarist_id
WHERE s.chord_complexity = 'high';

    (3, 9, 2, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'high', 210),
    (4, 9, 3, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'medium', 78),
    (5, 9, 4, 'Wave', 'high', 95),
    (6, 9, 4, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'medium', 38),
    (7, 11, 1, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'high', 150);

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE analyze(IN recital INTEGER)
BEGIN
    SELECT experience_level,
           AVG(transition_ms) AS avg_transition_ms
    FROM complex_chord_shifts
    WHERE recital_id = recital
        AND song_name = 'Girl from Ipanema'
    GROUP BY experience_level
    ORDER BY avg_transition_ms;

    SELECT DISTINCT g.name AS guitarist_name
    FROM chord_shifts s
        JOIN guitarists g
            ON g.guitarist_id = s.guitarist_id
    WHERE s.recital_id = recital
        AND s.chord_complexity = 'medium'
        AND s.transition_ms < 50
    ORDER BY guitarist_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL analyze(9);

Schema: Bugs (bug_id INT, title VARCHAR, description TEXT, status VARCHAR, assigned_to_user_id INT), Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. Select all bugs and their assigned users.
2. Find all bugs with a specific status (e.g., 'Open').
3. Count the number of bugs assigned to each user.
4. Create a new bug report.
5. Update the status of a bug.
text_nat:
SELECT
    b.bug_id,
    b.title,
    b.description,
    b.status,
    u.username AS assigned_to_username,
    u.email AS assigned_to_email
FROM
    Bugs AS b
LEFT JOIN
    Users AS u ON b.assigned_to_user_id = u.user_id;

SELECT
    bug_id,
    title,
    description,
    status
FROM
    Bugs
WHERE
    status = 'Open';

SELECT
    u.username,
    COUNT(b.bug_id) AS bug_count
FROM
    Users AS u
LEFT JOIN
    Bugs AS b ON u.user_id = b.assigned_to_user_id
GROUP BY
    u.username
ORDER BY
    bug_count DESC;

Schema: Players (player_id INT, username VARCHAR, join_date DATE), Games (game_id INT, game_name VARCHAR, genre VARCHAR), Scores (score_id INT, player_id INT, game_id INT, score INT, score_date DATETIME).

Queries:
1. Select all players and their highest scores in any game.
2. Find all scores for a specific game (e.g., 'Space Invaders').
3. Calculate the average score for each player.
4. Add a new player.
5. Record a new game score.
text_nat:
-- 1. Select all players and their highest scores in any game.
SELECT
    P.username,
    MAX(S.score) AS highest_score
FROM
    Players P
JOIN
    Scores S ON P.player_id = S.player_id
GROUP BY
    P.username;

-- 2. Find all scores for a specific game (e.g., 'Space Invaders').
SELECT
    P.username,
    S.score,
    S.score_date
FROM
    Players P
JOIN
    Scores S ON P.player_id = S.player_id
JOIN
    Games G ON S.game_id = G.game_id
WHERE
    G.game_name = 'Space Invaders'
ORDER BY
    S.score DESC;

-- 3. Calculate the average score for each player.
SELECT
    P.username,
    AVG(S.score) AS average_score
FROM
    Players P
JOIN
    Scores S ON P.player_id = S.player_id
GROUP BY
    P.username;

Queries:
1. List all members whose membership is currently active.
2. Count the number of books currently on loan by each member.
3. Find books that are overdue (ReturnDate is NULL and DueDate is past).
4. Register a new member and record a book loan for them.
5. Update the 'ReturnDate' for a specific book loan.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all members whose membership is currently active.
SELECT MemberID, FirstName, LastName
FROM Members
WHERE MembershipEndDate >= CURDATE() OR MembershipEndDate IS NULL;

-- 2. Count the number of books currently on loan by each member.
SELECT m.FirstName, m.LastName, COUNT(l.BookID) AS BooksOnLoan
FROM Members AS m
JOIN Loans AS l ON m.MemberID = l.MemberID
WHERE l.ReturnDate IS NULL
GROUP BY m.MemberID, m.FirstName, m.LastName;

-- 3. Find books that are overdue (ReturnDate is NULL and DueDate is past).
SELECT b.Title, b.Author, l.BorrowDate, l.DueDate
FROM Books AS b
JOIN Loans AS l ON b.BookID = l.BookID
WHERE l.ReturnDate IS NULL AND l.DueDate < CURDATE();

-- 4. Register a new member and record a book loan for them.
INSERT INTO Members (FirstName, LastName, MembershipStartDate, MembershipEndDate)
VALUES ('Jane', 'Doe', CURDATE(), '2025-12-31');

INSERT INTO Loans (MemberID, BookID, BorrowDate, DueDate, ReturnDate)
SELECT MemberID, 101, CURDATE(), DATE_ADD(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 14 DAY), NULL
FROM Members
WHERE FirstName = 'Jane' AND LastName = 'Doe';

-- 5. Update the 'ReturnDate' for a specific book loan.
UPDATE Loans
SET ReturnDate = CURDATE()
WHERE LoanID = 5; -- Assuming LoanID 5 is the specific loan to update

Queries:

3. List technicians who have resolved more than 20 tickets this month.
4. Create a new ticket for a user and assign it to a technician.

text_nat:
SELECT
  T.TicketID,
  T.Subject,
  T.Description,
  U.Username
FROM Tickets AS T

  T.Status = 'Open' AND T.Priority = 'High' AND U.Department = 'Finance';

  ON Tec.TechnicianID = Tic.AssignedTo
WHERE
  Tic.Status = 'Resolved' AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', Tic.CreatedDate) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m', 'now')
GROUP BY
  Tec.TechnicianID,
  Tec.FirstName,
  Tec.LastName

  ResolvedTicketsCount > 20;

text_es: Schema: Rooms (room_id, room_name, capacity), Bookings (booking_id, room_id, user_id, start_time, end_time, purpose). Queries: 1. Find all available rooms for a specific time slot. 2. text_nat:
-- 1. Find all available rooms for a specific time slot
SELECT
  R.room_id,
  R.room_name,
  R.capacity
FROM
  Rooms AS R
WHERE
  R.room_id NOT IN (
    SELECT
      B.room_id
    FROM
      Bookings AS B
    WHERE
      (
        '2023-10-26 10:00:00' < B.end_time
        AND '2023-10-26 11:00:00' > B.start_time
      )
  );

-- 2. List all bookings made by a particular user
SELECT
  booking_id,
  room_id,
  start_time,
  end_time,
  purpose
FROM
  Bookings
WHERE
  user_id = 101;

VALUES

SET

WHERE
  booking_id = 5;

-- 5. Get the total number of bookings per room
SELECT
  R.room_name,
  COUNT(B.booking_id) AS total_bookings
FROM
  Rooms AS R
LEFT JOIN
  Bookings AS B
ON
  R.room_id = B.room_id
GROUP BY
  R.room_name
ORDER BY

    S.role,

FROM

JOIN
    Departments AS D
ON
    S.dept_id = D.dept_id
GROUP BY

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
select
    C.title,
    C.department,
    C.credits
from
    Courses as C
join
    Enrollments as E on C.course_id = E.course_id
where
    E.student_id = 101;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
select
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name,
    S.major
from
    Students as S
join
    Enrollments as E on S.student_id = E.student_id
where
    E.course_id = 201;

-- 3. Enroll a student in a new course.
insert into Enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
values (103, 203, '2024-03-15', null);

-- 4. Update a student's grade for a course.
update Enrollments
set grade = 'A'
where student_id = 101 and course_id = 201;

-- 5. Count the total credits a student is enrolled in.
select
    sum(C.credits) as total_credits
from
    Enrollments as E
join
    Courses as C on E.course_id = C.course_id
where
    E.student_id = 101;
